name: Kupiah meukeutop
note: A traditional Acehnese head covering for men.

name: Kain endek
note: Balinese weavers use the weft-ikat technique to create patterned endek cloth.

name: Mi Bangka
note: This Bangka noodle specialty reflects Hakka culinary influences.

name: Tempoyak
note: In Bengkulu, fermented durian is used in sambal and fish dishes.

name: Rabeg
note: This richly spiced meat dish is associated with Serang and Banten’s sultanate cuisine.

name: Ilabulo
note: Sago and chicken offal are seasoned and wrapped in banana leaves.

name: Nasi gemuk
note: This coconut-milk rice is a familiar breakfast in Jambi.

name: Surabi Sunda
note: Sundanese rice-flour pancakes cooked in clay vessels, with sweet or savory toppings.

name: Pangsi Betawi
note: Betawi pangsi outfits come in colors including black, red, white and green.

name: Songket Sambas
note: Gold- and silver-coloured threads enrich this Sambas Malay ceremonial textile.

name: Zapin Tembung
note: Zapin Tembung is a social dance in West Kalimantan’s cultural repertoire.

name: Musik Sampe
note: This plucked Dayak instrument accompanies music and customary activities, with names varying by community.

name: Mak Yong
note: In the Riau Islands, Mak Yong theater brings together acting, dance, and music.

name: Teater Mamanda
note: This traditional theatre stages royal stories with familiar character roles and lively audience interaction.

name: Tari Giring-giring
note: This Ma’anyan dance uses sticks to express joy at welcomes, harvest celebrations and customary gatherings.

name: Festival Iraw Tengkayu
note: Tarakan’s Tidung celebration includes a decorated ceremonial boat and a ritual offering to the sea.

name: Tari Sigeh Pengunten
note: This Lampung welcome dance honors guests and draws on Pepadun and Saibatin traditions.

name: Ikan kuah kuning
note: Turmeric and citrus season the yellow fish soup served alongside papeda.

name: Tari Soya-Soya
note: This energetic martial dance is linked to the history of the Ternate Sultanate.

name: Sate rembiga
note: These beef skewers from Rembiga near Mataram have a spicy, savory and slightly sweet marinade.

name: Caci Manggarai
note: This Manggarai performance in Flores features a whip-and-shield duel accompanied by song, gongs and drums.

name: Hidangan bakar batu
note: Dani cooks use heated stones in an earth oven to cook tubers and meat for communal feasts.

name: Pangan sagu Bariat
note: Afsya families in Bariat, South Sorong, process sago from their customary forests as a staple.

name: Sagu sep (Marind)
note: Marind cooks in Merauke prepare sagu sep with sago and grated coconut using hot stones.

name: Bolu kemojo
note: This dense Riau cake takes its name from a frangipani-like flower shape.

name: Bumbu woku
note: Minahasan woku uses aromatic herbs and spices for fish, seafood or chicken.

name: Dendeng balado
note: Thin slices of beef are paired with a chili sauce in this Minangkabau dish.

name: Kasoami
note: A cassava-based staple sold in Muna communities such as Lohia.

name: Konro
note: A Makassar beef-rib soup with a dark, spiced broth.

name: Jepa
note: A cassava-and-coconut flatbread from the Mandar culinary tradition.

name: Songket lepus
note: Lepus songket appears in the ceremonial clothing of Palembang brides and grooms.

name: Pakaian kulit kayu Ranta
note: In the Bada Valley, traditional barkcloth clothing is known as ranta.

name: Arsik
note: This Batak fish dish is seasoned with andaliman and aromatic spices.

name: Gamelan gaya Yogyakarta
note: Yogyakarta’s court tradition preserves a distinctive style of Javanese gamelan.
